Settled per PSP but the bank credit falls in the next cycle. A date-blind rule reads this as a loss; it is only timing.

Sub-rupee (0.50) rounding drift — clean, but above the 0.01 exact-fee tolerance, so a strict rule still routes it.
PSP marks the payment refunded but the ledger still shows 'paid'.
Refund handled correctly on both sides; refund debit narrated as a refund — must NOT be flagged.
A properly reflected refund whose bank debit quotes the payment id — a substring rule mistakes it for a chargeback.
Settled then reversed; the debit references the payment id — textbook chargeback.
A real chargeback whose debit omits the payment id — a narration-substring rule never sees it and calls the order clean.
A bank credit whose settlement ref matches no known settlement — a genuine unmatched credit.
The bank typed the settlement ref in a different case (SETL_ vs setl_). An exact-string match loses the tie on both the order and the credit.
